## Build and run

### Dependencies (this section was generated by AI)

The project requires GNU Make, a C compiler, Python 3 for the self-check, and
the OpenSSL development headers and crypto library. On Ubuntu or WSL Ubuntu,
install the packages with:

```bash
sudo apt update
sudo apt install build-essential libssl-dev python3
```

Build both programs from this directory:

```bash
make build
```

Start the server in one terminal. It creates the root directory if needed:

```bash
make run-server PORT=5000 ROOT=server-files
```

Run a client in another terminal. Replace `YOURNAME` with a printable client
name of 1–32 bytes:

```bash
./etp-client --host 127.0.0.1 --port 5000 --name YOURNAME list
./etp-client --host 127.0.0.1 --port 5000 --name YOURNAME get REMOTE_NAME LOCAL_PATH
./etp-client --host 127.0.0.1 --port 5000 --name YOURNAME put LOCAL_PATH REMOTE_NAME
```

Run the course self-check from this directory with:

```bash
make check
```

## What works and what does not

The client implements the `list`, `get`, and `put` commands. The server handles
ETP sessions, serves files from its configured root, and uses a separate thread
for each client connection.

**Self-check results:**

Execution: 30 / 30 points

|---|---|
| `src/client.c` | Client command handling and ETP session logic for `list`, `get`, and `put`. |
| `src/server.c` | Server command handling, client sessions, file operations, and response logging. |
| `src/etp.c` | ETP message framing, header handling, filename validation, and SHA-256 helper. |
| `src/transport_tcp.c` | TCP listen, accept, connect, exact send/receive, and close operations. |

| `include/transport.h` | Transport interface used by the client and server. |

| `evidence/pa1-capture.pcap` | 200-byte-snaplen packet capture containing the PUT and GET sessions. |
| `evidence/time-wait.txt` | `ss` output showing TIME-WAIT for the captured connections. |
| `evidence/ANALYSIS.md` | Packet facts and analysis of the GET session. |
